liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): Relaxed version with strong vocals from Jerry and Donna; the closing ooh-oohs sound soulful and ghostly; Second set is on fire from He's Gone through Around and Around [10][11]
- **Werewolves In London** (2 reviews): Noted as the first Werewolves; Jerry's singing is badly off time, but his slide playing redeems the blown verses; Reviewer hears this as the first Werewolves, and thinks Jerry sounds very high [6][8]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Likes the Bertha into Good Lovin' opener, followed nicely by Friend of the Devil [8]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Friend of the Devil, Passenger and Candyman are called sweet first-set cuts [11]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Soft, sweet version; the band brings it way down near the last verse with quiet drums, guitar and bass [14]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the highest-energy Deal they have heard from the band [16]
- **It Must've Been the Roses** (1 other source): Seed discs for this song came from Charlie Miller (FOB) [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Werewolves In London**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 12 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-19.sbd.gans.miller.9121.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 171 min; rated 4.69/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the sound and mentions a corrected file order compared with the other source; Sound detail on the drums, space and Other One stretch is exceptional, especially on Grado headphones; Stereo separation puts keys in the left ear and Jerry's guitar in the right [8][9][10][15]
- **gd1978-04-19.mtx.seamons.94522.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd78-04-19.sbd.murphy.7286.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 171 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this the best-sounding of all the April shows they have heard, which all sound lovely [5]
- **gd1978-04-19.fob.sonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.94494.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [4]

## Around the show

- Werewolves of London is listed as the encore [3]
- A tape flip occurs at the start of Around and Around [4]
- The second-set track titles are shifted: Deal is unlisted, so Samson is actually Deal, though the text file is right [5]
- Second-set titles are off because Deal is missing from the listing, bumping every later song down [6]
- Bertha into Good Lovin' openers were common in 1978; the reviewer cites 2/3 and 2/5 '78 as other great ones [11]
- Reviewer says it stands out even among the Spring '78 shows [15]
- Reviewer considers it one of the finest shows for Donna they have found [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-19.sbd.gans.miller.9121.shnf**: source: SBD>Rm>CD>David Gans Sonic Solutions>CD [1]
- **gd1978-04-19.mtx.seamons.94522.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Sony ECM-250 recording onto cassette master (Sony TC-158, Maxell UDXL-II90), played on Nakamichi DR-1 into Sound Devices 744T at 24bit/96k, then edited and made FLAC16; Joani Walker recorded the show and Paul Scotton supplied audience tapes. Charlie Miller did the transfers and mastering, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; Hunter made a matrix mix that adds crowd ambiance to the soundboard [2][14]
- **gd78-04-19.sbd.murphy.7286.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Gans; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard-era MSR source went to DAT, then Sonic and CD, mastered by David Gans; The shn files came from Bob Murphy, with a partial retrack by Darrin Sacks; Identified by the reviewer as a Gans tape [3][13]
- **gd1978-04-19.fob.sonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.94494.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [4]. Also: Tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [4]
